business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business section.
business_model.claim: Encore's core business is purchasing portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts from credit originators (banks, credit unions, consumer finance companies, commercial retailers) and collecting on them over time.
quotes: We primarily purchase portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and manage them by working with individuals as they repay their obligations and work toward financial recovery.
Defaulted receivables are consumers' unpaid financial obligations to credit originators, including banks, credit unions, consumer finance companies and commercial retailers.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: A secondary revenue stream is fee-based debt servicing and portfolio management for non-performing loans in Europe, provided to credit originators.
quotes: We also provide debt servicing and other portfolio management services to credit originators for non-performing loans in Europe.
Servicing revenue consists primarily of fee-based income earned on accounts collected on behalf of others, primarily credit originators.

business_model.basis: Stated in both the 10-K MD&A and the Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: The company reports three business segments: MCM (United States), Cabot (Europe), and LAAP (Latin America and Asia-Pacific).
quotes: Encore Capital Group, Inc. ("Encore") has three business units: MCM, which consists of Midland Credit Management, Inc. and its subsidiaries and domestic affiliates; Cabot, which consists of Cabot Credit Management Limited and its subsidiaries and European affiliates, and LAAP, which is comprised of our investments and operations in Latin America and Asia-Pacific.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A revenue table and 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Portfolio revenue, the accretion of the discount on the negative allowance at an effective interest rate, is the largest component of total revenue, representing 82.3% of 2025 revenues and 81.4% of Q2 2026 revenues.
quotes: (1) Portfolio revenue, which is the accretion of the discount on the negative allowance due to the passage of time (generally the receivable portfolio balance multiplied by the EIR)

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A revenue table and 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Changes in recoveries, comprising over/under-performance versus forecast and changes in expected future recoveries, is the second revenue component, adding $208,771 thousand in 2025 (11.8% of revenues) and $71,115 thousand in Q2 2026 (14.5% of revenues).
quotes: (2) Changes in recoveries, which includes: (a) Recoveries above (below) forecast, which is the difference between (i) actual cash collected/recovered during the current period and (ii) expected cash recoveries for the current period, which generally represents over or under performance for the period; and (b) Changes in expected future recoveries, which is the present value change of expected future recoveries

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A and 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Total debt purchasing revenue (portfolio revenue plus changes in recoveries) accounted for 94.1% of 2025 total revenues and 95.9% of Q2 2026 total revenues.
quotes: Total debt purchasing revenue | 1,664,566 | 94.1%

business_model.claim: Collections are executed through three channels: call center and digital collections, legal collections, and collection agencies.
quotes: We utilize three channels for the collection of our receivable portfolios: call center and digital collections; legal collections; and collection agencies.

business_model.claim: In the U.S., the majority of portfolio purchases come from forward flow agreements with credit originators, typically committed early in the calendar year, with defined volume, frequency, and pricing over three to twelve months.
quotes: A "forward flow" contract is a commitment to purchase receivables over a duration that is typically three to twelve months, but can be longer, with specifically defined volume, frequency, and pricing.

The majority of our deployments in the U.S. come from forward flow agreements, and the timing, contract duration, and volumes for each contract can fluctuate leading to variation when comparing to prior periods.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A portfolio pricing discussion.
business_model.claim: U.S. portfolio supply and pricing are key revenue drivers: elevated lending and charge-off rates keep supply robust and pricing favorable, while in Europe competitive pricing constrains the capital Encore elects to deploy.
quotes: With lending and charge-off rates remaining near recent peak levels, U.S. portfolio supply continues to be robust.
portfolio pricing remains competitive across our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we elect to deploy in Europe.
